title: Highly-Multiplexed Tissue Imaging with Raman Dyes
protocol: Prepare the conjugation buffer as ~0.1 M NaHCO3 in PBS buffer, pH = 8.3.
Store the conjugation buffer at 4 °C.
Prepare N-hydroxysuccinimidy (NHS) ester-functionated MARS probe solution as 3 mM in anhydrous DMSO.
Store the dye NHS ester solution protected from light and kept at -20 °C.
Dissolve antibody solids in the conjugation buffer to a concentration of 2 mg/mL.
For antibodies dissolved in other buffers, exchange them into the conjugation buffer using centrifugal filters to achieve a concentration of 1-2 mg/mL.
Add 15-fold molar excess of dye solution to the antibody solution slowly with stirring.
Incubate the reaction mixture at room temperature with stirring for 1 h, protecting it from light.
Prepare the slurry of gel filtration resin in PBS buffer.
Add 10 mL of gel filtration resin powder into 40 mL of PBS buffer inside a 50-mL tube.
Keep the solution in a 90 °C water bath for 1 h.
Decant the supernatant and re-add PBS to 40 mL.
Store the slurry at 4 °C.
Pack the size exclusion column with the slurry solution to the height of 10-15 cm.
Rinse and wash the column with ~10 mL of PBS buffer to further pack the resin.
Pipette the conjugation reaction mixture (~0.5 mL) to the column.
Immediately add 1 mL of PBS buffer as the elution buffer when all reaction mixture is loaded.
Constantly refill the elution buffer (PBS) to the column.
Collect the eluate of the conjugate solution by looking at the color on the column or measuring the absorbance at 280 nm.
Concentrate the collected solution to 1-2 mg/mL with a centrifugal filter.
Determine the concentration and the average degree of labeling (DOL, dye-to-protein ratio) by measuring the ultraviolet-visible (UV-Vis) spectrum of the conjugate solution with a Nano plate reader.
Anesthetize the mice with isoflurane.
Assess proper anesthetization using a toe pinch test.
Kill the mice by cervical displacement.
Perfuse the mice transcardially with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS.
Collect the mouse brain as described in steps 2.1.4-2.1.5.
Cut upward from the brain stem along the sagittal suture.
Peel the two halves of the skull away to the side.
Scoop out the brain with a tweezer.
Fix the collected brain in 4% PFA in PBS at 4 °C for 24 h.
Wash the brain in PBS buffer at 4 °C for 24 h to remove excess PFA.
Place solid agarose into water to achieve a final concentration of 7% (w/v).
Stir the solution with a glass stirring rod.
Heat the slurry in microwave until clear.
Allow the agarose to cool to 45-55 °C.
Pour the liquid agarose into a small chamber.
Transfer the brain from PBS to the liquid agarose and orient it with a spatula to embed the brain.
Wait for the tissue-agarose block to harden.
Section the tissue-agrose into 40-µm-thick coronal slices using a vibratome.
Transfer the tissue to a 4-well plate for staining.
Remove the agarose from the tissue with a tweezer.
Wash the tissue with 1 mL of PBS three times.
Fix mouse pancreata in 4% PFA in PBS at 4 °C with rocking for 16-20 h.
Wash the sample in 1 mL of PBS (at 4 °C) three times to remove PFA.
Embed the sample (~0.3-0.5 cm in size) in OCT compound blocks.
Place 2 drops of OCT into a plastic cryomold.
Position the tissue correctly and cover it with OCT until no part is exposed.
Section the pancreata to 8-µm-thick slices.
Immobilize the sections onto a tissue binding glass slide.
Store the slides in -80 °C.
Equilibrate the specimen to room temperature before staining.
Wash the tissue with PBS to remove OCT blocks.
Bake the FFPE tissue slide at 60 °C for 10 min.

Place samples sequentially in xylene two times, ethanol two times, 95% ethanol in deionized water two times, 70% ethanol in deionized water two times, and 50% ethanol in deionized water one time, each for 3 min at room temperature with mild shaking.
Transfer the sample into 20 mM sodium citrate (pH 8.0) at 100 °C in a glass jar.
Ensure tissues are immersed in the solution and place the jar in a 60 °C water bath for 45 min.
Wash the sample with deionized water at room temperature for 5 min.
Draw a boundary around the tissue sections on the slide using a hydrophobic pen.
Incubate the tissues with 0.3-0.5% PBST (Triton X-100 in PBS) for 10 min.
Incubate the tissues with blocking buffer (5% donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 30 min.
Prepare the primary staining solution by adding all primary antibodies to 200-500 µL of staining buffer (2% donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS).
Centrifuge the primary staining solution at 13,000 x g for 5 min.
Use only the supernatant if precipitates form.
Incubate the tissue in the primary antibody solution at 4 °C for 1-2 days.
Wash the slides three times with 0.3-0.5% PBST at RT for 5 min each.
For floating tissues, use 1 mL PBST for washing.
Ensure all tissues on the slide are immersed in the solution during washing.
Incubate the tissue in 200-500 µL of blocking buffer for 30 min.
Prepare the secondary staining solution by adding all secondary antibodies and lectins if required to 200-500 µL of staining buffer at desired concentrations (normally 10 µg/mL).
Centrifuge the secondary staining solution at 13,000 x g for 5 min.
Use only the supernatant if precipitates form.
Incubate the tissues in 200-500 µL of secondary antibody solution at 4 °C for 1-2 days.
Wash the slides twice with 0.3-0.5% PBST at RT for 5 min each.
Incubate the tissue with 200-500 µL of DAPI solution for 30 min.
Wash the slides three times with PBS at RT for 5 min each.
Transfer floating tissue sections to glass slides with a glass-dropping pipette.
Spread the tissue on the slide with a tissue brush.
Clean the surrounding of the tissue with wipes if needed.
Mount the tissue in a drop of antifade reagents and cover it with a glass coverslip.
Secure the coverslip with nail polish.
Prepare a vibration-isolated optical table in a room with temperature control.
Place a synchronized dual-laser system on the optical table with a chiller connected.
Mount mirrors with wavelength range 750-1100 nm.
Mount dichroic beam splitters with 980 nm long-pass filter using kinematic mounts.
Measure height of laser output and sizes of pump and Stokes beams.
Adjust mirrors and lenses to ensure light hits center of optical elements.
Place mirror M1 on the optical table at approximately 45° to the laser output.
Make tip and tilt adjustments using knobs on kinematic mount for M1.
Ensure light travels along the length of the table in a straight line.
Place and align dichroic beam splitters and mirrors to split pump and Stokes beams.
Place and align lens pairs L1, L2, and L3, L4 to collimate beams and expand diameters.
Use mirrors M7 and M8 to align combined laser beams into the microscope.
Align one beam into the microscope first using mirror pairs for spatial overlap.
Set up detection part by placing an infrared-coated oil condenser with 1.4-NA.
Mount a large-area Si photodiode onto a shielded box with BNC connectors.
Add a 64-V DC power supply to the mounted photodiode.
Reflect the forward-going light with a 2-inch mirror.
Refocus the light onto the photodiode after an optical filter that blocks the modulating Stokes beam.
Send the output current of the photodiode to a fast lock-in amplifier terminated with 50 ohms for signal demodulation.
Send an 8-MHz trigger to the lock-in amplifier as the reference signal.
Send the in-phase X-component of the lock-in amplifier into the analog interface box of the microscope.
Optimize the temporal overlap with the built-in motorized delay stage by measuring the SRS signal of pure D2O liquid at the microscope.
Set laser power to Ppump = 10-40 mW and PStokes = 40-80 mW on the laser control panel.
Set pixel dwell time to 2-4 µs using the microscopy software.
Use multiple frames averaging typically 10-20 frames.
Avoid a combinatorial use of high laser power (Ppump > 40 mW, PStokes > 80 mW) and small pixel size (<0.2 µm).
Set the time constants of the lock-in amplifier to half of the pixel dwell time.
Perform linear spectral unmixing.
